3aa9964ac35bc994.heading: Averaging for creators of literary or artistic works (Self Assessment helpsheet HS234)

amounts.name: Averaging profit variance threshold
amounts.value: less than 75% of the profits of the other tax year, or one tax year's profits are nil

caveats: Cannot claim averaging if the cash basis was used to calculate profits.
Cannot claim if business started or ended in 2024 to 2025 or 2025 to 2026, or if a partner joined/left the partnership in those years.

Averaging does not affect tax/NIC actually payable for earlier years - adjustments are made via the 2024 to 2025 tax and NIC calculation (chunk text as given, though example references suggest interplay with 2025-26 figures - see Section 11 which states adjustment is via 2025 to 2026 liability).

If profits for either year later change, a previously made averaging claim is ignored and must be reclaimed via amendment or, if the amendment time limit has expired, by writing to HMRC without delay due to a time limit.
Where Making Tax Digital for Income Tax applies, claims/adjustments are made through compatible software rather than the SA boxes referenced in this helpsheet.

definitions.meaning: A relief for creators of literary or artistic works allowing them to add together profits for 2 years and be taxed on the average, to smooth fluctuating results, subject to conditions.
Profits from disposing of works or royalties for allowing reproduction of works, e.g. authors selling written work or software writers earning royalties on copyrighted code.
Profits from services provided rather than from the works themselves, e.g. architects or programmers paid for services even if some work is copyright-protected.

obligations.must: Enter the increase/decrease in box 72 of Self-employment (full) pages
Enter the increase/decrease in box 11 of Partnership pages
Pay tax and National Insurance contributions for earlier years in full even if averaging reduces profit for those years

obligations.deadline: Time limit for amending tax return (not specified in chunk); if expired, write to HMRC without delay due to a time limit
obligations.must: Amend tax return to reclaim averaging on changed profits, or write to HMRC if amendment time limit has expired
obligations.trigger: Profits for 2025 to 2026 or 2024 to 2025 change
obligations.who: Taxpayer whose profits change after averaging claim

note.summary: HS234 explains the special averaging relief for authors and artists with fluctuating profits, allowing them to average profits over two tax years (2024 to 2025 and 2025 to 2026) if the difference exceeds 75% or one year's profit is nil. It sets out eligibility (income from disposal/royalties of works, not services), exclusions (cash basis users, businesses that started/ended or partners who joined/left in the relevant years), how to compute profit for sole traders and partners using specific box references, how to claim (box 72 for sole traders, box 11 for partners), worked examples, and how changes in profit or claim amendments after the time limit are handled.
